'''Jennifer A. Flegg''' is an Australian [[mathematician]] and professor of [[applied mathematics]] in the School of Mathematics and Statistics at the [[University of Melbourne]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://findanexpert.unimelb.edu.au/profile/762115-jennifer-flegg|website=Find an Expert at the University of Melbourne|access-date=2025-11-29|title=Profile: Prof Jennifer Flegg}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Flegg received her PhD in Applied Mathematics from [[Queensland University of Technology]] in 2009. Her dissertation, "''Mathematical Modelling of Chronic Wound Healing",'' was supervised by Dr. Sean McElwain.<ref>{{citation |title=Mathematical modelling of chronic wound healing |author=Jennifer Flegg |url=https://eprints.qut.edu.au/40164/ |publisher=Queensland University of Technology |accessdate=30 April 2021}}</ref> From 2010 to 2013, she was a researcher at the [[University of Oxford]] developing mathematical models for the spread of resistance to [[antimalarial drug]]s. From 2014 to early 2017, she was a mathematical lecturer in the School of Mathematical Sciences at [[Monash University]]. In May 2017, she joined the School of Mathematics and Statistics at the [[University of Melbourne]] as a senior lecturer in Applied Mathematics and was promoted to associate professor in 2020 and again to Professor in 2022.<ref>{{citation |title=Professor Jennifer Flegg |url=https://www.iddo.org/professor-jennifer-flegg |publisher=Infectious Diseases Data Observatory |accessdate=10 December 2025}}</ref>

Flegg is an expert in the field of [[Mathematical and theoretical biology|mathematical biology]], with special focus in infectious disease [[epidemiology]], [[wound healing]] and [[Neoplasm|tumor]] growth.

As of 2020, Flegg also serves as an editorial board member for [[PLOS Computational Biology]], [[eLife]] and the [[Bulletin of Mathematical Biology]].

==Awards and honors==

In 2020, Flegg was awarded the JH Michell Medal for excellence in research by [[ANZIAM]] (Australian and New Zealand Industrial and Applied Mathematics),<ref>{{Cite web|title=ANZIAM : The 2020 JH Michell Medal|url=https://www.anziam.org.au/The+2020+JH+Michell+Medal|access-date=2021-04-08|website=www.anziam.org.au}}</ref> as well as the Christopher Heyde Medal<ref>{{Cite web|title=Christopher Heyde Medal {{!}} Australian Academy of Science|url=https://www.science.org.au/christopher-heyde-medal|access-date=2021-04-09|website=www.science.org.au|language=en}}</ref> from the [[Australian Academy of Science]] and the Society of Mathematical Biology.
In 2025, Flegg was awarded the EO Tuck Medal by the [[Australian Mathematical Society]] in recognition of her outstanding research and distinguished service to the field of applied mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Professor Jennifer Flegg awarded the EO Tuck Medal|url=https://ms.unimelb.edu.au/about/news-and-events/professor-jennifer-flegg-awarded-the-eo-tuck-medal|access-date=2025-04-10|website=www.ms.unimelb.edu.au|language=en}}</ref> She was elected a [[List of fellows of the Australian Academy of Science|Fellow of the Australian Academy of Science]] in 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jen Flegg |url=https://science.org.au/about-us/academy-fellows/discover-our-fellows/jen-flegg |access-date=2026-05-22 |website=Australian Academy of Science}}</ref>
